text.title: Remote 1:1 Async Fallback Core Rules
text.summary: 9 testable rules every remote 1:1 async fallback application MUST enforce. HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override them.

rule.statement: An async cycle MAY be posted only when a synchronous 1:1 is infeasible for that specific cycle (no overlapping working hours, one party on temporary leave, sickness, travel) and the note records which reason applies. A pair MUST NOT run more than 3 consecutive async cycles without a synchronous call; when timezones make weekly sync structurally impossible, the pair schedules a sync call at least once every 4 cycles outside one party's normal hours by rotation.

rationale.source: GitLab Handbook, asynchronous communication guidance; Horstman, The Effective Manager (Wiley, 2016)

rule.rationale: Async 1:1s are cheaper for the PM, so without a cap they quietly become the default and the relationship degrades into a form. Voice and video carry the hesitation, the pause and the "actually, one more thing" that a doc never does; the methodology exists to preserve signal during gaps, not to replace the meeting.

rule.statement: Every note MUST carry exactly the three named prompts `blockers`, `decisions_needed` and `morale`, each at least 10 characters and each asking for a specific, answerable thing (a WBS or ticket id, a decision owner and date, numeric 1-10 scales). The morale prompt MUST use the same axes as the team's pulse survey (workload, autonomy, clarity) so answers are comparable across cycles. Generic prompts ("anything to share?", "how is it going?") are rejected.

rationale.source: Widely established practice in structured 1:1s; Horstman, The Effective Manager (Wiley, 2016)

rule.rationale: A vague prompt gets "all good" as a reply and the PM learns nothing. Fixed, specific prompts do two things: they make a two-minute reply useful, and they make cycle N comparable with cycle N-4, which is the only way a slow slide in clarity from 8 to 5 becomes visible before the resignation.

rule.statement: `response_window_business_hours` MUST be between 24 and 168, published in the note at posting time, and counted in the IC's working days and timezone, never the PM's. Public holidays and formal leave days in the IC's location do not count toward the window. The default is 48 business hours; a shorter window than 24 is invalid even if both parties agree.

rationale.source: Widely established practice in cross-timezone remote management (GitLab Handbook, asynchronous communication)

rule.rationale: A 48-hour window posted at 17:00 Friday PM-time is a Monday-morning deadline for an IC ten hours ahead, which reads as "answer over your weekend". Counting in the IC's hours is what makes the window a fair contract rather than a pressure tool, and it is what keeps the unresponsive count honest.

rule.statement: A cycle counts as answered only when `ic_response.received_at` is inside the window and all three fields are present. An empty or "nothing" answer to a prompt is valid; an absent field, or a reply in a different channel that was never copied into the note, is not. The PM MUST NOT fill `ic_response` on the IC's behalf from a chat or hallway conversation.

rationale.source: Widely established practice in written 1:1 protocols

rule.rationale: "No blockers" is information; a missing blockers field is silence, and the two must not be confused when the count that drives escalation is computed. Letting the PM transcribe a Slack thread into the note turns the IC's record into the PM's paraphrase, and the morale field in particular must stay in the IC's words.

rule.statement: The PM MUST write `pm_ack` within 24 business hours of `ic_response.received_at`. Every item in `next_actions` MUST carry `action`, `owner_role` and `deadline_sprint`. If the IC reported a blocker or a decision needed, `next_actions` MUST NOT be empty; an ack of "thanks, noted" with no action against a reported blocker is invalid.

rationale.source: Horstman, The Effective Manager (Wiley, 2016), on 1:1 follow-through; widely established practice

rule.rationale: The async format removes the moment where the IC watches the PM write something down. If the reply to "PR review stalled 3 days" is a thumbs-up, the IC learns that the note is a ritual and stops reporting blockers; the owned, dated action is the only visible proof the note was read.

rule.statement: When the window closes without a valid response, `unresponsive_count` MUST be incremented and `escalation.action` set: count 1 sets `synchronous_reschedule` (a sync slot offered within the next cycle); count 2 or more sets `escalate_to_manager` and the PM MUST NOT post another async note until synchronous contact has been made. `action: none` with an expired window is invalid. A valid in-window response resets the count to 0.

rationale.source: Widely established practice in remote people management (silence as a leading indicator)

rule.rationale: Two missed cycles from an IC who used to reply in an hour is the earliest signal a PM gets of burnout, a job search or a conflict with the PM themselves; a third async note into that silence is the PM protecting their own calendar. The ladder converts silence into a required human contact rather than a growing number in a JSON file.

rule.statement: A cycle that overlaps the IC's formal leave (vacation, parental, sick leave per company policy) MUST be recorded as paused, not posted; it does not increment `unresponsive_count` and the PM MUST NOT send reminders or DMs about the note during leave. The next cycle after return restarts the count at its pre-leave value.

rationale.source: Right-to-disconnect legislation (France, Loi Travail 2016, art. L2242-17; Australia, Fair Work Act right to disconnect, 2024)

rule.rationale: An unanswered note during vacation is not an unresponsive cycle, and escalating it to the IC's manager is how a fallback protocol becomes a grievance. In several jurisdictions the reminder itself is a compliance problem; in all of them it is a trust problem.

rule.statement: The note MUST live in a channel visible only to the PM and the IC (private doc, DM, or email thread), one note per pair per cycle. Morale answers MUST NOT be copied into team-visible reports, dashboards or the IC's performance file; the quarterly review MAY report morale only as a pair-level trend or an aggregate across at least 5 ICs. The IC's manager, when escalated to, receives the unresponsive count and the last acked next_actions, not the morale field.

rationale.source: Widely established practice in 1:1 confidentiality; Horstman, The Effective Manager (Wiley, 2016)

rule.rationale: The morale scale is honest for exactly as long as the IC believes it stays between the two of them. The first time a "clarity 4" shows up in a leadership deck with the IC's name attached, every subsequent answer from every IC on the team is a 7.

rule.statement: Every 90 days at most the PM MUST compute the in-window response rate over the quarter's cycles per pair. A rate below 80% over any 4 consecutive cycles MUST produce a recorded decision: change the response window, restructure the pair, or mandate synchronous 1:1s for that pair. The review bumps `header.version` and `last_reviewed`; a note computed under a `last_reviewed` older than 90 days is invalid.

rationale.source: Deming PDCA cycle; widely established practice in operating-cadence review

rule.rationale: A pair that answers 3 of 8 notes is not being served by the async protocol, and the protocol will not fix itself. The 80% line and the forced decision turn a slowly failing pair into a structural conversation instead of a year of half-empty notes.

section.title: Conclusion targets used by the decision tree

rule.statement: Run the full procedure; emit an artefact passing the output contract.
rule.rationale: Terminal target used by 06-decision-tree when preconditions hold.

rule.statement: Skip; surface the missing precondition; do not synthesize.
rule.rationale: Terminal target used by 06-decision-tree when preconditions fail.
